title: Gorilla Permits for Groups in Rwanda Come in Blocks of Eight, and That Shapes the Whole Trip
meta_title: Gorilla Permits for Groups: Rwanda Booking Guide
meta_description: Gorilla permits for groups in Rwanda: how many families you need, deposits, the 30% low-season discount and rescheduling rules. Plan your group trek.
excerpt: Gorilla permits for groups in Rwanda are issued eight per gorilla family a day, so large parties need several families, early bookings and a clear payment plan.
content:
Gorilla permits for groups in Rwanda are booked in blocks of eight, because Volcanoes National Park lets only eight visitors spend an hour with each habituated gorilla family a day. A group of 16 needs two families on the same morning; a group of 30 needs four. Each permit costs US$1,500 per foreign non-resident (checked November 2026).

For a club, company or extended family, that eight-person rule shapes the whole trip: the dates, the hotels, the transport and the budget. This guide covers how many families your group needs, when to book, the deposit and rescheduling rules, and the trek day itself. It is one part of our wider advice on how to organise a group safari in East Africa.

Quick Facts

  • Permit price: US$1,500 per foreign non-resident, with lower promotional rates for African and EAC travellers (checked November 2026)
  • Group size per family: 8 visitors per habituated family per day, for one hour
  • Families open to visitors: 12 fully habituated families in Volcanoes National Park, about 96 permits a day in total
  • Minimum age: 15 years on the day of the trek
  • Low-season discount: 30% off from November to May with two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe
  • Trek start: 7am briefing at the park headquarters in Kinigi, about 2.5 hours by road from Kigali

How Do Gorilla Permits for Groups Work in Rwanda?

Gorilla permits for groups work exactly like individual permits: each trekker needs a named permit for a specific date in Volcanoes National Park. What changes is the arithmetic, because no gorilla family can take more than eight people a day.

The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) sells permits through its online portal and through licensed tour operators. Gorilla permits for groups are issued one per person in each traveller's name, so collect full names and passport details for every member before anything is confirmed. The Visit Rwanda gorilla tracking page sets out the core rules, and our guide to the Rwanda gorilla permit covers prices and discounts for individual travellers.

Gorilla permits for groups are capped at eight per family

Volcanoes National Park has twelve fully habituated gorilla families that receive visitors, and RDB issues eight permits for each family each day. That gives roughly 96 permits a day for the whole country, so a group of 20 would use more than a fifth of the daily supply. This is why gorilla permits for groups sell out on particular dates long before solo travellers notice.

Who decides which family your group visits?

The park staff at Kinigi allocate families on the morning of the trek, after the briefing, and they try to match each sub-group to a family whose location suits its fitness. Your driver-guide can pass on requests, such as a shorter walk for older members, but gorilla permits for groups are for the park, not a named family. Treks can take anything from 30 minutes to four hours or more, between about 2,500 and 4,000 metres above sea level.

How Many Gorilla Families Does a Large Group Need?

A large group needs one gorilla family for every eight trekkers, rounded up. Ten people need two families, 17 need three, and 40 would need five of the twelve families on one day, which is rarely realistic unless gorilla permits for groups are booked many months ahead.

Group sizeFamilies neededHow the day usually works
Up to 81The whole group treks together, sometimes with no other visitors
9 to 162Two sub-groups leave Kinigi at the same time and trek to different families
17 to 243Three sub-groups; split by walking pace so each ranger sets a comfortable speed
25 to 404 to 5Usually better spread over two trekking days, with half the group on another activity
More than 406 or morePlan two or three trekking days; one day would take half the park's permits

A sub-group that does not fill all eight places shares its family with other visitors. A group of 12 split into two sixes will probably trek with strangers in both; splitting 8 and 4 keeps one sub-group private.

The same logic applies across the border, and our post on group gorilla trekking in Uganda explains how Bwindi's sectors change the picture if your numbers outgrow Rwanda.

When Should a Group Book Rwanda Gorilla Permits?

A group should book as soon as the dates and a realistic headcount are agreed. Six months or more ahead is sensible for June to September and the weeks around Christmas, when demand tends to be highest, and even quieter months can fill on specific dates once several families are needed at once.

The usual mistake is waiting for every last name before booking. Secure gorilla permits for groups on the number you are confident of, then add places if more people join. Dropping a permit later costs money, so a cautious first number is safer.

Advance booking with a deposit

RDB offers licensed tour operators an advance booking service: the operator checks availability and holds the date by paying 40% to 99% of the permit fee, then pays the balance before 30 days to the trek. For gorilla permits for groups, this is the most useful tool, because it locks in several families on one date before every traveller has paid in full.

Advance bookings made this way can be moved free of charge, as long as the change is made 30 days or more before the booked date. Miss that window and an unconfirmed advance booking expires, so put the balance deadline in your own calendar as well as your operator's.

Splitting a big group across two trekking days

For groups of 25 or more, two trekking days are often easier than one. Half the group treks on day one while the rest do golden monkey trekking, a Dian Fossey campus visit or a village walk, and the roles swap the next morning. This also halves the pressure on vehicles and lodges.

What Do Gorilla Permits for Groups Cost?

Gorilla permits for groups cost the same per person as individual permits, because RDB has no group or trade rate. At US$1,500 per foreign non-resident (checked November 2026), they are usually the largest single cost of a group trip to Rwanda, so budget for them first.

Group sizePermits at US$1,500With the 30% low-season discount
8 trekkersUS$12,000US$8,400
12 trekkersUS$18,000US$12,600
16 trekkersUS$24,000US$16,800
24 trekkersUS$36,000US$25,200

These figures cover gorilla permits for groups only, worked out from the published per-person fee; vehicles, lodges, guides and tips come on top. A 40% advance deposit for 16 people is US$9,600, worth knowing before you set your members' payment dates.

The low-season discount for a whole group

From November to May, RDB takes 30% off a gorilla permit for travellers who also stay in Akagera or Nyungwe. Each person needs either two paid nights in one of those parks, or one night in each on consecutive nights, plus one paid activity there. One qualifying stay unlocks one discounted permit per person, and cash payment at the park is not accepted. Check the current RDB low-season discount rules before you quote your members.

For gorilla permits for groups, this discount can pay for much of the extra time in another park. Our 6 day Rwanda celebration safari already includes two nights at Magashi Camp in Akagera before the gorilla trek, the kind of shape that can qualify between November and May.

Rates for African citizens and residents

Mixed groups often include Kenyan, Ugandan or other African members, and gorilla permits for groups can mix rates. Under RDB's promotional rates, announced in January 2026 and running until 31 December 2026, Rwandans and EAC citizens pay US$200 and African citizens and residents US$500, though not between June and October 2026. Confirm each passport's rate before splitting costs.

Rescheduling, Cancellations and No-Shows in a Group

Rwanda gorilla permits are not refunded once paid, but a confirmed permit can be moved to another date for a fee of 20% of the permit price. With gorilla permits for groups, that rule matters most when one or two people drop out close to the trek.

  • Rescheduling more than 7 days ahead: approved automatically once the 20% fee is paid.
  • Rescheduling within 7 days: possible only with RDB approval, so it is never guaranteed.
  • No-show on the day: the permit is treated as expired, with nothing to transfer or recover.
  • Advance bookings with a deposit: free to move if changed 30 days or more before the date.

The practical answer is travel insurance for every member that covers prepaid activities. Our travel insurance guidance explains what to look for.

Tell members early that a place cannot simply be handed to a friend. If someone withdraws, ask your operator what RDB will allow before promising a swap.

Planning the Trek Day and the Rest of the Itinerary

The trek day starts early. Every sub-group must be at the Volcanoes National Park headquarters in Kinigi for the 7am briefing, so most groups sleep in the Musanze and Kinigi area the night before rather than driving from Kigali that morning.

Vehicles, porters and pace

Plan one vehicle per sub-group, matching the number of families on your gorilla permits for groups, so each can leave its trailhead independently. Porters can be hired at the start of each trek to carry day packs and help on muddy slopes. Before the trip, share our honest look at how hard gorilla trekking is so each member can tell the guide which pace suits them.

Building the days around the permits

Kigali to the park is about 2.5 hours by road, while Akagera to Volcanoes is about five hours, so groups combining the two need a full travel day. A short corporate group can follow the shape of our 5 day Rwanda incentive safari, while a longer trip can add Akagera before the trek and finish on Lake Kivu. Our group safaris pages cover clubs, families, schools and corporate groups in more detail.

If you are a travel agent booking on behalf of clients rather than leading your own group, our guide to booking gorilla permits as a tour operator explains the trade side of the same rules.

Insider Tips

  • Book on a firm number: Hold gorilla permits for groups on the headcount you are sure of; adding later is easier than paying to move
  • Split by pace, not by friendship: Sub-groups that walk at the same speed enjoy the trek more and reach the gorillas fresher
  • Watch the 30-day line: Advance deposits must be topped up, or moved, before 30 days to the trek
  • Use the low season: November to May can cut each permit by 30% if every member spends two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe
  • Check ages: Every trekker must be at least 15 on the day; plan another activity for younger family members

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a group of more than eight trek the same gorilla family in Rwanda?

No. Rwanda issues only eight gorilla permits per habituated family per day, so more than eight people cannot visit one family together. Gorilla permits for groups larger than eight are spread across two or more families on one morning, or across two days, each sub-group with its own ranger guide.

How far ahead should a large group book gorilla permits in Rwanda?

A large group should book Rwanda gorilla permits as soon as the travel dates and a realistic headcount are agreed, ideally six months or more ahead for June to September and the Christmas weeks. Big groups need several families on one date, and partly sold-out days are the main reason group dates have to move.

How much do gorilla permits for groups cost in Rwanda?

Gorilla permits for groups cost the same per person as for anyone else: US$1,500 per foreign non-resident trekker (checked November 2026). There is no group rate, so a party of 16 pays US$24,000 in permits alone. From November to May the 30% low-season discount can bring each permit down to US$1,050 if its conditions are met.

Does the Rwanda low-season discount work for a whole group?

Yes, the Rwanda low-season discount can apply to every member of a group, as long as each person meets the conditions. Between November and May, each trekker needs two paid nights in Akagera or Nyungwe, or one night in each consecutively, plus one paid activity. Each qualifying stay unlocks one discounted gorilla permit per person.

What happens if someone in our group cancels after the permits are paid?

A paid Rwanda gorilla permit is generally not refunded if one person in the group cancels, and a no-show on the day means the permit is treated as expired. A confirmed permit can be moved to a new date for a fee of 20% through RDB, so ask your operator early whether rescheduling suits that traveller.

Final Thoughts

Gorilla permits for groups come down to three numbers: eight people per family, about 96 permits a day, and US$1,500 per foreign non-resident. Work out how many families your group needs, hold the dates with a deposit, and build the rest of the trip around those mornings in Kinigi.
